scope: Full-Swift offscreen first-snapshot attribution and ordered encoder experiment on macOS
environment: arm64 macOS 27.0.1, Swift 6.3.3 full WASI SDK, Rust 1.99.0 release VM

measurement.conclusion: Most of the generic encoder work moved to the first list load. The complete journey showed no repeatable CPU gain. Compare both phases in the mobile replay.

ios265.environment: One owned iPhone 15 arm64 Simulator on iOS 26.5. Both comparator builds declare iOS 17.0.
ios265.sampling: Fresh application processes on one boot, alternating which arm led. Executable and Wasm bytes checked after each install. One-minute host load varied from 73.64 to 100.53 on 15 logical cores.
ios265.cleanup: Owned Simulator observed absent. External inventory unchanged.

androidAPI28.environment: One owned arm64 API 28 emulator boot, original 30-second owner deadline, byte-identical ELF and 17 runtime libraries across arms.
androidAPI28.steadyRSS: All four guest runs hit the deadline before a steady-state sample.
androidAPI28.cleanup: All four guests closed with zero live ledger counters and tickets. Emulator and private ADB groups observed absent. Scratch removed.

fullPathHostFollowup.scope: Five alternating fresh arm64 macOS pairs with Swift 6.3.3 WASI and Rust 1.99.0 release VM
fullPathHostFollowup.decision: Keep the full-path encoder opt-in. Save regressed in all five pairs. Continue full-Swift VM optimization before building another mobile comparison.

limits: The baseline was rebuilt because the historical mobile Wasm was unavailable. The mobile candidate encodes the first diagnostic snapshot. These offscreen comparisons missed the 200 ms startup target, and the time to the first usable list had no consistent improvement. Signed activation, iOS 17.x runtime and product p95 remain open.
cleanup: All 47 command groups settled. Disposable build, cache and attribution overlay removed.
